messages.content: Write a post about starting a mentorship program on an engineering team. Around 250 words.

output:
**We started a mentorship program. Here's what I'd do differently.**

Six months ago three of our juniors were quietly stuck. Not failing — shipping, passing review, showing up. Just not getting any better, and nobody had noticed because their PRs were fine.

So we paired each of them with a senior engineer. Thirty minutes a week, on the calendar, non-negotiable.

The first version was bad. We told the pairs to "meet and discuss growth," which produced eight weeks of polite status updates. Mentorship without an agenda decays into a second standup.

What fixed it was giving every pair one artifact to work on together. A design doc the mentee was writing. A gnarly bug in a service they'd never touched. A promo packet, drafted out loud. Something with edges. The conversation stopped being about career trajectory in the abstract and started being about why this retry loop swallows the error.

Two other things mattered. We let people opt out of a match without explaining themselves — one pair had zero chemistry and both were too polite to say so for a month. And we asked the seniors what they wanted from it, which surfaced that half of them saw mentoring as unpaid overhead until we made it count in their own reviews.

Results after two quarters: two of the three juniors are now leading features end to end. The third moved to a different team, which I count as a win.

The whole thing costs about two hours a week of senior time. We should have done it a year earlier.
